## Build and Version Note {.unnumbered}

- **Generated:** 2026-09-26
- **Source verification:** Primary and roadmap sources for Chapters 1-8 and the series-wide topic roadmap were last verified between 2026-09-22 and 2026-09-26.
- **Release status:** Complete content draft (release candidate 7) -- all 8 chapters drafted; release candidates 2-6's fixes are preserved. This revision corrects release documentation inaccuracies in RC6 where the typography mechanism was misdescribed. Chapters 4 and 7 titles use inline Typst code (#linebreak()) for parser-safe line breaks, eliminating mid-word hyphenation while preserving the RC5 Chapter 8 subsection-rendering fix. This remains a review artifact, not the final edition -- see the release-candidate note earlier in this book for what (if anything) is still outstanding.

### Provenance {.unnumbered}

- Tied-embeddings usage (Chapter 2) has no dedicated primary source; the sandwich-norm claim (Chapter 2) leans on a secondary source rather than a model's own technical report. Both are tracked sourcing gaps, not unsupported claims.
- All worked-example numbers in Chapters 1-8 (attention weights, parameter counts, KV-cache sizes, receptive fields, MoE parameter/routing counts, ch. 6's hypothetical-config GQA group size, ch. 7's two-model resource diagnosis, ch. 8's looped-vs-unrolled depth arithmetic) are computed by version-controlled project scripts and checked by the project's automated test suite, not hand-derived.
- Figures are generated from version-controlled scripts using a fixed visual-style configuration, not drawn freehand; each figure's caption credits its scholarly/technical source where one applies.
- Chapter 8 is this workbook's assigned primary home for recurrent depth/looped transformers. Its two verified examples (Mixture-of-Recursions, a research proposal; Nanbeige4.2-3B, a released open-weight model) were each verified via full-text PDF extraction. Public reporting associating recurrent depth with 'GPT-6 Astra' is explicitly treated as unconfirmed, not verified fact, everywhere it is mentioned.
- Chapter 8's MTP bridge and Chapter 7's MTP/speculative-decoding cross-reference are both deliberately shallow -- MTP's training mechanics and the speculative-decoding algorithm are assigned to future workbooks, not taught in workbook 4.
- Chapter and Answer Key numbering: the eight instructional chapters are numbered 1-8; front matter (how to use this workbook, the notation quick reference), the answer keys, and this build note are intentionally unnumbered so the rendered numbering matches the book's logical structure, and each chapter's rendered title carries exactly one leading number.
- The notation reference's cache-size row names M_KV (the standard MHA/MQA/GQA cache formula) and M_MLA (MLA's compressed-latent cache formula) to match the symbols the equations actually use, and adds the sliding-window width W, referenced throughout that chapter's worked example and questions.
